Quick Look in History

Press Space on any capture in the History grid to peek at it — full size, without opening an editor. The same gesture you already know from Finder.

  • Space to preview, Space or Esc to dismiss: screenshots open as images, recordings play in the native Quick Look player with standard controls. Clicking a capture still opens the Editor or Trim Editor, exactly as before.
  • Arrow keys ride along: the grid gains keyboard focus — arrows move the selection ring through your current search results (only what's visible, never the full archive), and an open preview follows it. Return opens the focused capture in its editor.
  • Right-click → Quick Look is there too, so the shortcut is learnable.
  • Honest about missing files: previewing an entry whose file was deleted behind Snapline's back answers with a clear message naming the capture — never a broken icon, never silence.

Fixes

  • Thumbnail previews keep their full Retina backing — capture cards no longer render at half resolution on Retina displays.
  • The Open confirmation for a scanned code's link is now a standard app-modal alert.

A license key confirmed to be circulating publicly no longer verifies; its owner received a free replacement. Replacement keys are always free from support.

QR codes and barcodes

Snapline now reads QR codes and barcodes in your captures — on-device, alongside text recognition.

  • Codes section in the Text window: every detected code is listed with its payload and a Copy button. Link payloads get an Open button that always shows you the full URL before anything opens.
  • Search by payload: a URL or ticket number that exists in a capture only as a code now finds that capture in History search.
  • Older captures: open a capture's Text window and use Re-scan to detect codes in captures taken before this update.

Snapline 2.4.0

  • Measure tool — a new editor tool (M) reads distances straight off a capture: drag to draw a ruler line with endpoint ticks and a live length label. Hold Shift to snap to 0/45/90°, and drag either endpoint later to re-measure — the label follows.
  • Pixels or points — the label reads in device pixels, or in points on captures that recorded their display's scale (new captures do, automatically). A 100-pt span captured on a Retina display reads 200 px or 100 pt, your pick; the toggle sits in the tool options. Older and imported captures keep the pt toggle visibly disabled rather than guessing a scale that could read wrong.
  • The outlined label stays legible over any content — light, dark, or busy — and measurements survive export and History re-edit as editable shapes, like every other annotation.
